subject: Parse error when truncating cauchy distribution

messages.author: ca8c217f8754f02e
messages.subject: Parse error when truncating cauchy distribution
parts:
I am trying to use a truncated cauchy distribution (to define a variance variable), however, I am getting a parse error with it (I took the code directly from from Reference guide on page 41). If I switch to a different distribution such as the normal, then everything seems to work fine. Removing the truncation also solves the parsing issue.


Here's the relevant code:

parameters {
 real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
 sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5) T[0,];
}

and here's the error

PARSE DID NOT SUCCEED.
ERROR: non-whitespace beyond end of program:
LOCATION: file=input; line=1, column=1


 ^-- starting here


DIAGNOSTICS FROM PARSER:


no matches for function name="cauchy_cdf"
    arg 0 type=int
    arg 1 type=int
    arg 2 type=real
lower truncation not defined for specified arguments to cauchy
Parser expecting: "}"


Any suggestions?

Thanks,
Ilya

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Parse error when truncating cauchy distribution
parts:
On Thursday, November 22, 2012 12:38:49 PM UTC-5, Ilya Esteban wrote:
I am trying to use a truncated cauchy distribution (to define a variance variable), however, I am getting a parse error with it (I took the code directly from from Reference guide on page 41). If I switch to a different distribution such as the normal, then everything seems to work fine. Removing the truncation also solves the parsing issue.

I guess we do not have a truncated Cauchy distribution yet. But in this case, explicit truncation is not necessary because the support of sigma matches the untruncated mass and the parameters to the Cauchy distribution are given. In other words, the integral always evaluates to 0.5 in this case, and Stan only needs to know the log-posterior up to a constant. There is more detail about this topic at the end of

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/VonPUkdcZuUJ

Ben

messages.author: ca8c217f8754f02e
messages.subject: Re: Parse error when truncating cauchy distribution
parts:
That worked, thank you.

Another observation regarding Cauchy distribution is that it seems much much slower than the Normal. I have a simple regression model with around 1000 covariates.  If I use the Normal distribution for the coefficients, it takes around 30 mins to complete 4 chains of 10000 iterations each. Switching to the Cauchy distribution it took a few hours to complete just 10% of the first chain, at which point I gave up. Sampling from the Cauchy also seems to slow down when a small value scale parameter is used (e.g. sampling from Cauchy(0,1) is much faster than Cauchy(0, 1e-6)

Thanks,
Ilya
